in_hebrew.name: ערטמוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the root 'artem' meaning 'two' and 'maseh' meaning 'strong'.

in_greek.name: Αρτέμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek goddess Artemis, meaning 'butcher', 'hunter', 'goddess of wilderness', or 'goddess of the hunt'. In the New Testament, it is the name of a disciple of Jesus.

in_latin.name: Artemus
in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Artemis', which is a translation of the Greek goddess Artemis.

biblical_reference.note: Artemas was a disciple of Jesus and a companion of St. Luke. He was probably the same person as the one named Drusus in Acts 16:1, and was possibly the bearer of the letter from the church at Ephesus to Paul in Acts 27:1-26.
